recommended_build_path.overall_recommendation: Do not treat current public NJ TRANSIT geometry as a full production-final network footprint. The best verifiable public path today is a partial official-map-and-facility build covering rail, light rail, stations, terminals, and other named NJ TRANSIT facilities; keep the row broad until a live official route-stop feed or equivalent downloadable system geometry is restored.
why_this_is_best_current_path: A former NJ TRANSIT developer GTFS lane is referenced by NJ TRANSIT's own 2010 announcement, but the current public developer path `https://www.njtransit.com/developer` returns `404 Not Found`.
The current live public system-map page exposes official statewide and light-rail PDFs that are usable for manual georeferencing of rail and major facilities.

The NJ TRANSIT Police district page and district PDF remain useful semantic evidence, but both returned Cloudflare `403` responses to automated `HEAD` requests on 2026-03-24 and should not be treated as stable automated download inputs.
include: NJ TRANSIT commuter-rail alignments visible on the official statewide system map PDF
NJ TRANSIT light-rail alignments from the Hudson-Bergen, Newark Light Rail, and River Line PDFs
rail and light-rail stations, named terminals, and named transit centers shown on the official map PDFs
other individually named NJ TRANSIT facilities that can be tied to official NJ TRANSIT map labels or facility pages
exclude: the full State of New Jersey polygon
any single county or place proxy
generalized statewide bus street coverage inferred only from a small-scale system overview map
ordinary bus-stop and route geometry unless an official downloadable route-stop feed is recovered
transformation_assumptions: Georeference the statewide and light-rail PDFs and vectorize rail and light-rail centerlines.
Convert mapped stations and terminals into point or small-area facility footprints; use modest station buffers only where the source gives a point-like label rather than a facility polygon.
Treat the police district map as semantic QA for named facilities and regional span, not as a literal county polygon input.

If bus-route geometry remains unavailable from official downloadable sources, do not fabricate a statewide bus network footprint from the overview map; leave the bus component unresolved rather than inventing false precision.
recommended_build_path.production_decision: Not fully production-usable from current public official geometry alone. The recommended operational posture remains broad overlap unless a restored authenticated GTFS or equivalent official route-stop export is obtained.

recommended_build_path.overall_recommendation: Use WMATA's official GTFS static feeds as the primary geometry source, with the combined rail-and-bus GTFS as the preferred base. Add official parking-facility inventory from WMATA's parking-details page, and use the Compact plus jurisdiction-boundary PDF only for legal QA and clipping logic, not as the footprint polygon itself.
why_this_is_best_current_path: The live WMATA developer portal documents an official `Rail & Bus Combined GTFS Static` operation and a rail-only GTFS static operation.
The live WMATA developer home page states that the GTFS feed includes platforms, levels, pathways, and more precise stop locations, which materially improves station-footprint building.
The official parking-details page is a live inventory of stations with parking, addresses, and lot or garage presence.
The Compact provides the legal definition of transit facilities and the explicit `150-foot` Metrobus stop-sign jurisdiction rule, which supports a defensible bus-stop treatment.
include: WMATA rail guideway from GTFS rail shapes
rail stations, platforms, pathways, and entrances represented in the GTFS-enhanced station model
Metrobus stop-sign areas using GTFS stop coordinates with a `150-foot` buffer consistent with the Compact
official station parking, park-and-ride, lot, and garage facilities from the WMATA parking-details inventory once geocoded or parcel-matched
other clearly WMATA-controlled rail or bus facilities that can be tied to official inventories
exclude: the entire WMATA jurisdiction boundary polygon
the broader `1,500 square mile` transit zone as a routine footprint polygon
generic buffers around every bus route segment between stops unless the segment itself is an official WMATA facility
transformation_assumptions: Acquire the combined GTFS through a WMATA developer subscription or authenticated pull step; the portal is live, but anonymous `HEAD` requests to the raw GTFS ZIP URL returned `404` on 2026-03-24.
Buffer rail alignments modestly to approximate trackway or right-of-way rather than treating centerlines as zero-width.
Union platform, pathway, and entrance features into station-area polygons before block-group weighting.
Geocode or parcel-match parking-facility addresses from `parking-details.cfm` to avoid using large station-wide buffers where a real parking facility can be located.
Use the jurisdiction-boundary PDF only as a QA envelope to catch obviously out-of-scope geometry, not as the final footprint.
recommended_build_path.production_decision: Production-usable once the GTFS pull is authenticated. This is the strongest near-exact public path for WMATA; no county or place surrogate should be used.

recommended_build_path.overall_recommendation: Build the UTA footprint from the official GTFS static feed, then add official station and park-and-ride facilities from UTA's station-address and park-and-ride inventory pages. This is a production-usable near-exact public build path.
why_this_is_best_current_path: UTA exposes a live public GTFS ZIP with routes, shapes, stops, trips, and stop_times.
UTA publishes a live official station-address inventory grouped by FrontRunner, TRAX Blue, TRAX Red, TRAX Green, and S-Line stations.
UTA publishes a live official park-and-ride inventory with named facilities and street addresses.
include: all active UTA route shapes and stop locations from GTFS
FrontRunner, TRAX, S-Line, bus, and BRT service elements represented in GTFS
rail stations and transit centers from the official station-address inventory
UTA park-and-ride facilities from the official park-and-ride inventory
non-rail UTA park-and-ride facilities that are clearly UTA-operated
exclude: the union of UTA member counties or cities
LDS church parking entries listed on the park-and-ride page unless separate evidence shows UTA property control
broad service-area polygons with no UTA route, station, stop, or facility presence
transformation_assumptions: Use GTFS shapes as centerlines and apply modest buffers for rail rights-of-way or route influence where needed for block-group weighting.
Use GTFS stops first for station coordinates, then use the station-address page to QA station identity and to promote major stations and transit centers into facility footprints.
Geocode park-and-ride street addresses or parcel-match them to create lot polygons; use conservative lot buffers only when no parcel geometry can be linked.
Do not elevate church-owned shared parking entries to police-property surfaces without explicit UTA control evidence.
recommended_build_path.production_decision: Production-usable now from public official sources. This is a strong candidate for custom-footprint implementation.

recommended_build_path.overall_recommendation: Build the BART police footprint from BART's official GTFS permalink plus BART's official stations-tracks-entrances KMZ. Use the KMZ as the primary exact geometry for tracks and station entrances, and use GTFS as the stable service and stop companion. This supports a production-grade system-property footprint across the full BART system, not an Alameda-only proxy.
why_this_is_best_current_path: BART publishes a no-registration GTFS permalink and explicitly documents it on the GTFS developer page.
BART publishes a current KMZ package containing stations, tracks, and station entrances, which is stronger geometry than GTFS stops alone.
The BART geospatial developer page is a stable official catalog for the KMZ assets.
include: the full current BART rail network across all served counties, using official track geometry from the KMZ
station entrances and station complexes from the KMZ
GTFS stops and shapes for QA, stop IDs, and service alignment checks
station-linked parking or access facilities only where an official station or parking inventory can be tied to a real parcel or named facility
exclude: union of all BART-served counties as a polygon proxy
fabricated parking-lot polygons unsupported by official geometry or a parcel-linked official inventory
transformation_assumptions: Use the KMZ `tracks` layer as the authoritative linear geometry and apply a modest guideway buffer for weighting.
Union station-entrance points by station and combine them with station centroids or GTFS stop groupings to form station-area facility polygons.
Use GTFS only as a companion QA and service table source where the KMZ already supplies better geometry.
If parking is added, require a station-linked official inventory plus parcel or address resolution; otherwise keep the parking component out rather than inventing lot shapes.
recommended_build_path.production_decision: Production-usable now from public official sources. This is the cleanest exact public geometry path among the four reviewed cases.
